Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE Opinion NO. 48 s. 2011 AUG O Z 2011 BtVAHENG ATTY. JOSE LUIS G. MONTALES Officer-in-Charge OFFICE OF THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR CITY GOVERNMENT OF TAGUIG Dear Atty. Montales: This has reference to your letter dated 18 July 2011 wherein you requested for opinion on nine (9) legal issues pertaining to the issuance and subsequent revocation of the locational clearance, zoning certification, building permit, and business permit of an establishment owner, Atty. George A. Elias. In your letter, you mentioned that the cause of revocation of the aforesaid permits were for non-compliance with application and registration requirements and the willful misrepresentation made by Atty. Elias on the zoning classification of the land where his building is erected. Further, in the same letter, allegations were made on how Atty. Elias purportedly took advantage of his position as the current Vice Mayor and Presiding Officer of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Taguig to pass Resolution No. 27, Series of 2011 in a special session held which converted the area where Atty. Elias' building is located from a residential zone to a commercial one. You claimed likewise that said special session was a sham as it was called without the requisite quorunn to do business. To these statements, you raised nine (9) legal issues for this Department's opinion: 1. Whether reclassification of lands by an LGU should be made through an ordinance, not a mere resolution, and only after public hearings have been conducted. 2. Whether a mere Resolution, which purports to reclassify a land, validly coverts (sic) a "residential" lot into a "commercia/" one. Our Opinion: Section 20 of RA 7160 provides for the reclassification of land which may be validly made through an ordinance, passed by the sanggunian concerned after the conduct of public hearings held for that purpose. The local government units shall, in conformity with existing laws, continue to prepare their respective land use plans enacted through zoning ordinances which shall be the primary and dominant bases for the future use of land resources. (Section 20 [c], RA 7160)

3. 4. 12 The law made an express requirement for an ORDINANCE, not resolution, to be passed in order to authorize the reclassification of lands. Whether a special session of the Sangguniang Pan/ungsod can be validly called by less than a majority of the members thereof. Whether a special session of the Sangguniang Pan/ungsod can validly transact business despite the absence ofa quorum. Our Opinion: A special session may be called by the local chief executive or by a majority of the members of the sanggunian, when public interest so demands. We cite the case of Manuel E, Zamora vs. Gov. Jose R. Caballero, G.R. No, 147767, 14 January 2004 to explain further Queries nos. 3 and 4: "Quorum" is defined as that number ofnzentbers ofa body which, when legally assembled in their proper places, will enable the body to transact its proper business or that number which "lakes a lawful body and gives it power to pass upon a law or ordinance or do any valid act. "MAJORITY", when required to constitute a quorunt, jneans the number greater than half or more than half of any total. In fine, the entire membership must be taken into account in cotnputing the quorunt of the sangguniang panlalawigan, for while the constitution merely states that "majority of each House shall constitute a quorum," Section 53 of the LGC is more exacting as it requires that the "MAJORITY of the ALL MEMBERS ofthe sanggunian.... ELECTED and QUALIFIED" shall constitute a quorum. The qualification in the LGC that the majority be based on those "elected and qualified" was "leant to allow sanggunians to filliction even when not all ntembers thereof have been proclainzed. xxx the provision necessarily applies when, after all the ntembers of the sanggunian have assunzed office, one or sonte ofits ntentbers file for leave. xxx A sanggunian is a collegial body. Legislation, which is the principal fitnction and duty of te sanggunian, requires the participation ofall its Iltenzbers so that they "lay not only represent the interests of their respective constituents but also help in tlle Iltaking of decisions by voting upon every question put upon the body. The ACTS of only a part of the sanggunian done OUTSIDE the parameters of the legal provisions aforementioned are LEGALLY INFIRM highly questionable and are, intportantly, NULL AND VOID. And all such acts cannot be given binding force and effect for they are considered UNOFFICIAL ACTS DONE DURING AN UNAUTHORIZED SESSION. " (enzphasis and underscoring supplied)

5. 6, 7. 8. 9, 13 Whether the Vice Mayor and the members of the Sangguniang Pan/ungsod could be charged criminally and administratively when they invited or allowed a non- member not only to participate in a sham special session but also to vote for a resolution. Whether the Vice Mayor, acting as Presiding Officer of the Sanguniang (sic) Pan/ungsod, violated Republic Act No. 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act when he called and presided over a sham special session for the purpose of passing a Resolution that was deliberately intended for his pecuniary benefit? Whether the legitimate members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod and the usurper to the position of SK Federation President violated any criminal and administrative laws when the participated in a sham special session and passed and i//ega/ Resolution intended to circumvent Section 20 of the LGC Whether the wife of the Vice Mayor, a regular employee of the City Government of Taguig, is liable under Republic Act No. 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, for using her position to expedite the applications of George Elias Space Rental in the CPDO, LBO and BPLO. Whether the Vice Mayor and the SP members who voted for the reclassification Resolution may be held criminally and administratively liable for falsely misrepresenting to the local regulatory offices that a (sic) the "residential" lot owned by the Vice Mayor has been reclassified as "commercial". Our Opinion: To Queries No. 5 up to 9, Section 60 of RA 7160 enumerates the various grounds for disciplinary actions wherein an elective local official may be disciplined, suspended, or removed from office for committing such acts. For grounds mentioned in Section 60, and elective local official may be removed from office by order of the proper court. Section 61 up to 68 of RA 7160 and Rule XIX, Articles 124 to 132 provides for the procedures in filing and administrative complaint against erring elective local officials. your guidance, we quote in full Section 61 of RA 7160: "Section 61. Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints. - A verified cojnplaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follozvs: (a) A cotnplaint against anv elective official ofa province, a highlv urbanized city, an independent contponent city or component city sliall be filed before the Office of the President' (b) A conplaint against any elective official ofa ntunicipality sltall be filed before the sangguniang panlalawigan tvhose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President; and (c) A conwlaint against any elective barangay official shall be filed before the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned whose decision shall be final and executory.

In the event that an administrative complaint is filed against an elective official of a province, a highly urbanized city before the Office of the President, the latter as the Disciplining Authority, after the respondent official shall have filed his or her Answer, shall refer the case to this Department, as the Investigating Authority pursuant to Administrative Order No. 23, Series of 1992, to commence investigation, evaluate and determine whether a prima facie case exists to warrant the institution of a formal administrative proceedings. Considering this mandate and the probability that the Department may be involved in the legal issues you raised, it is proper that we defer to make any particular opinion on Queries No.5 up to 9. On your query involving erring employees whose acts are not sanctioned under Sections 61 to 68 of RA 7160, the determination as to whether probable cause or prima facie case exists to hold them liable for acts violative of any law, statute, rules and regulations, lies within the proper agency charged with such duty such as the Office of the Ombudsman and the Civil Service Commission, among others. On the matter of the present controversy involving the SK Federation Presidency and the purported usurper, this Department is without authority to ADJUDICATE on matters that are properly within the ambit of the judicial courts or quasi-judicial bodies, and neither will it render an opinion on matters that are already the subject of a pending court case in keeping with the principle on sub judice. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Very truly yours, ATTY. JESUS B. q6QUE IV DIRECTOR 111 / LS:55/06
